intended_object: The canonical ℤ-linear isomorphism T_ℓ(V/L) = lim_n (V/L)[ℓ^n] (transition maps given by multiplication by ℓ) ≅ the (ℓ)-adic completion of L, for an abelian group V on which multiplication by ℓ is bijective. It sends a coordinate [v] at level n to [ℓ^n v] in L/ℓ^n L. Inferred from the docstring, the type and the companion eval lemmas.
explanation: The source type is the sections of the ℕᵒᵖ-diagram n ↦ ker(ℓ^n on V/L), with multiplication by ℓ as the transition maps; this is the inverse limit of the ℓ^n-torsion, i.e. the Tate module. The target is Mathlib's AdicCompletion (span{ℓ}) L. The lemma scalarTorsionEquivAdicCompletion_eval confirms the map is the one in the docstring: [v] ↦ [ℓ^n v] mod ℓ^n L. Mathematically this is a correct isomorphism. It is well defined because changing v by l ∈ L changes ℓ^n v by ℓ^n l ∈ ℓ^n L. It is compatible across levels because ℓv_{n+1} − v_n ∈ L, so ℓ^{n+1}v_{n+1} − ℓ^n v_n ∈ ℓ^n L. The inverse is a_n ↦ [ℓ^{-n} a_n], using bijectivity of ℓ on V. Degenerate cases are consistent: ℓ = 0 forces V = 0, and for ℓ = ±1 both sides are trivial. The ℤ-setting is the standard one for Tate modules. A version over a general commutative ring with an invertible scalar would be possible, but it is not the standard notion. Mathlib has no such comparison isomorphism; it only supplies the building blocks used here.
